title: In Psalms 83 How Can We Understand The Unity Of The Enemies Against Gods People In The Context Of Spiritual Warfare Today
paragraphs: Understanding Psalm 83: The Unity of God’s Enemies and Spiritual Warfare Today

Psalm 83 is a striking passage that portrays a coalition of nations uniting against Israel, God’s chosen people. This psalm, attributed to Asaph, is both a historical lament and a prophetic insight into the ongoing reality of opposition against God’s people. In this study, we will explore how the unity of these enemies can be understood not only in its immediate context but also through the lens of spiritual warfare, as it applies to believers today.
1. The Historical Setting of Psalm 83
The psalmist cries out to God regarding a confederacy of hostile nations plotting against Israel:

They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; That the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance. For they have consulted together with one consent; Against thee do they make a covenant: - Psalm 83:4-5 ASV

Here, we see a deliberate and unified effort to destroy Israel. The list of enemies in Psalm 83:6-8 includes ancient foes such as Edom, Moab, and Ammon. This coalition is not just a political alliance, but an alliance “against thee”—against God Himself, as the psalmist recognizes that to attack God’s people is to attack God’s purposes.
2. Spiritual Warfare: The Deeper Conflict

While the original context is historical, the unity of God’s enemies in Psalm 83 also illustrates a deeper spiritual principle. The New Testament reveals that believers are engaged in spiritual warfare against the forces of evil:

For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against the principalities, against the powers, against the world-rulers of this darkness, against the spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places. - Ephesians 6:12 ASV

Just as the nations united against Israel, the powers of darkness are unified in their opposition to God and His people. The enemy’s goal remains the same: to “cut them off from being a nation” and erase the testimony of God’s people. This unity is seen in Satan’s schemes to undermine the church, discourage believers, and oppose the advance of the gospel.
3. God’s Sovereignty and the Assurance of Victory
Despite the intimidating unity of the enemy, the psalmist turns to God for deliverance:
O my God, make them like the whirling dust; As stubble before the wind. - Psalm 83:13 ASV
This plea acknowledges human weakness and the necessity of divine intervention. The New Testament assures believers that victory is found not in human strength but in the Lord:
Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us. - Romans 8:37 ASV
God’s people are called to stand firm, clothed in the armor of God (Ephesians 6:13), trusting that He will ultimately defeat every enemy that rises against His kingdom.
4. The Purpose of the Struggle: God's Glory Revealed
The psalm ends with a prayer that God’s enemies would come to know His name and power:
That they may know that thou alone, whose name is Jehovah, Art the Most High over all the earth. - Psalm 83:18 ASV
Spiritual warfare is not just about survival; it is about the revelation of God’s glory. When believers stand firm in faith, the world sees the power and faithfulness of God.
5. Application for Today
Recognize the reality of spiritual opposition. The unity of the enemy is real, but so is the power of God.
Rely on God’s strength. Spiritual battles are won through prayer, faith, and dependence on God’s Word (Matthew 4:4).
Seek God’s glory above all. Pray that through every trial, God will be known as the Most High.
Conclusion

Psalm 83 reminds us that opposition to God’s people is ultimately opposition to God Himself. The unity of the enemy is formidable, but the unity and power of God’s people, grounded in Christ, is greater still. As we engage in spiritual warfare today, let us do so with confidence that the Lord fights for us, and His purposes will prevail.
